Benefit:

Ibn Abi al-Hadid said in (Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah) concerning this verse: The view of the majority of our companions (p-4813) is that the soul is a subtle, vapour-like body formed from the finest parts of nourishment, which penetrates the veins, inhering in them; and likewise for the heart, and likewise for the liver.

And according to them, the Angel of Death has assistants who seize the souls by way of deputizing for him; were it not so, it would be impossible for him, being a body, to seize two souls at one time in the east and the west, since one body cannot be in two places at one time.

Our companions said: It is not far-fetched that the recording angels (al-Hafazah al-Katibun) are the ones who seize the souls at the expiry of the term.

They said: The manner of seizure is that the angel enters from the mouth to the heart, since he is a subtle, airy body, not hindered from passing through narrow openings; so he mingles with the soul, which is like a resemblance to it, since it is vapour-like; then he exits from where he entered, and it is with him.

This occurs only at the time God Exalted permits him, which is the arrival of the term.

They were then obliged to hold that the angel would dive into water with the drowning person to seize his soul beneath the water. They accepted this, and said: It is not impossible for the angel to penetrate the water through the pores of the water, for in it there are pores and passages, and in every body, according to their principle of affirming pores in bodies.

They said: Even if we supposed there were no pores in it, it would not be far-fetched that the angel could enter it and make room for himself, just as stone and fish and others enter it, and like a strong wind that strikes the surface of the sea, hollowing and digging it out; and the power of the angel is stronger than the power of the wind. End.

The preferable course, regarding what one does not know the manner of, is to stop at what is recited and not go beyond it, out of good manners in avoiding rushing into the unseen, and scrupulousness in refraining from attempting what does not reach its reality, and following the example of those who went before who did not delve into it, and they are the elite and the exemplars. Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[23–24] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, so be not in doubt about meeting him, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ ﴿And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs.﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24]

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, that is, the Torah. ﴿So be not in doubt about meeting him﴾, that is, the meeting with the Book, which is the Qur'an. The pronoun refers back to the Book mentioned earlier, and what is meant is something other than it, by way of istikhdam (a figure of speech in which one pronoun carries two different referents). Alternatively, it refers to a known [specific] Book, or there is an omitted noun in the construction, meaning: "You receive its like," that is, "So be not in doubt about its being a revelation received from Him, exalted is He." The meaning is: "We gave Moses the like of what We gave you of the Book, and We caused him to receive revelation like what We caused you to receive, so be not in doubt that you have met its like."

The Prophet's ﷺ being forbidden from doubt is intended to forbid his community, and it is an allusion to those from whom something similar had proceeded. ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, that is, from misguidance. ﴿And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, leaders in goodness who called the creation to Our command and Our law. ﴿When they were patient﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, in acting upon it and holding fast to its commands. ﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, they affirmed with the utmost and most complete affirmation. The meaning is: "Thus We shall certainly make the Book which We gave you a guidance for your community, and We shall certainly make from among them leaders who guide with the like of that guidance."

It is understood from the implication of the verse that when the Children of Israel cast aside holding fast to the Book, and cast aside patience in enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and lost certainty in the truth of faith, they altered and changed [it], and that station was taken from them, and it was turned against them as retribution. This is His way, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]. Thus, within this encouragement lies a warning, and what a warning it is.

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[23–24] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, so be not in doubt about meeting him, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ ﴿And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs.﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24]

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, that is, the Torah. ﴿So be not in doubt about meeting him﴾, that is, the meeting with the Book, which is the Qur'an. The pronoun refers back to the Book mentioned earlier, and what is meant is something other than it, by way of istikhdam (a figure of speech in which one pronoun carries two different referents). Alternatively, it refers to a known [specific] Book, or there is an omitted noun in the construction, meaning: "You receive its like," that is, "So be not in doubt about its being a revelation received from Him, exalted is He." The meaning is: "We gave Moses the like of what We gave you of the Book, and We caused him to receive revelation like what We caused you to receive, so be not in doubt that you have met its like."

The Prophet's ﷺ being forbidden from doubt is intended to forbid his community, and it is an allusion to those from whom something similar had proceeded. ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, that is, from misguidance. ﴿And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, leaders in goodness who called the creation to Our command and Our law. ﴿When they were patient﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, in acting upon it and holding fast to its commands. ﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24], that is, they affirmed with the utmost and most complete affirmation. The meaning is: "Thus We shall certainly make the Book which We gave you a guidance for your community, and We shall certainly make from among them leaders who guide with the like of that guidance."

It is understood from the implication of the verse that when the Children of Israel cast aside holding fast to the Book, and cast aside patience in enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and lost certainty in the truth of faith, they altered and changed [it], and that station was taken from them, and it was turned against them as retribution. This is His way, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]. Thus, within this encouragement lies a warning, and what a warning it is.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 32, verses 25–27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25–27] ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ.﴾ ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs. Then will they not hear?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26] ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and themselves eat? Then will they not see?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 27].

﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge﴾, i.e., will decide, ﴿between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾, i.e., He will distinguish the truth from falsehood by distinguishing the one who is right from the one who is wrong. ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., let it become clear to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., those that passed away, with the destruction of annihilation. ﴿Among whose dwellings they walk﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., their homes, like the homes of the people of Shu'ayb, Hud, Salih, and Lut, peace be upon them. They do not see in them anyone from among those who used to inhabit and dwell in them; they went away as if they had never flourished therein, as He said: ﴿So those are their houses, ruined because of what they wronged﴾ [an-Naml: 52]. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., in what We did to them, ﴿are signs﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., lessons, admonitions, and corresponding proofs. ﴿Then will they not hear?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 26], i.e., the news of those who came before, how their affair turned out because of their denying the messengers and their transgression of corruption upon the earth, so that this would lead them to faith.

﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾ [al-Sajdah: 27], which is the land whose vegetation has been cut off, i.e., cut away. ﴿Thereby bring forth crops from which their livestock and themselves eat﴾ [al-Sajdah: 27], meaning grass, fruits, and herbs. ﴿Then will they not see?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 27], i.e., so that they may infer from it His perfect power and the necessity of His being singled out for divinity. This is like His saying: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾ [Abasa: 24] ﴿how We pour down water in torrents﴾ [Abasa: 25], and the verse [continues].

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28 - 29] ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, the disbelief of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 29]

﴿And they say﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿"When is this victory?"﴾, that is, the triumph over us. It is a demand for the arrival of the Lord's punishment that they were promised, and a deeming of it unlikely, ﴿"if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 29] because there will descend that which covers the sights and blinds the insights, and the signs of faith will appear, and the disbelieving faction will perish.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, when the might of Allah, His wrath, and His anger come upon you in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved﴾, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾ [Ghafir: 83] and the verse after it. Whoever claims that what is meant by this victory is the conquest of Makkah has gone far astray in his interpretation and erred gravely, for on the Day of Victory the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted the Islam of the Tulaqa' (the freed ones), and they were nearly two thousand. Had the intended meaning been the conquest of Makkah, he would not have accepted their Islam, given His saying: ﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them"﴾ [As-Sajdah: 29]. Rather, what is meant is the victory that is judgment and decision, as in His saying: ﴿Decide between me and them with a decision﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 118], and His saying: ﴿Say, "Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with truth"﴾ [Saba': 26], and the verse. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿They sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾ [Ibrahim: 15], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you seek a decision, the decision has certainly come to you﴾ [Al-Anfal: 19].

(p-4820) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.﴾

﴿So turn away from them﴾, that is, from the polytheists, and do not concern yourself with them, and convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. ﴿And wait﴾, that is, for victory over them, for Allah will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you, for He does not break His promise. ﴿Indeed, they are waiting﴾, that is, for what is in their souls, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ [al-Tur: 30] and ﴿They await for you misfortunes﴾ [al-Tawbah: 98]. That is, they will find the outcome of their waiting to be the dreadful consequence of His punishment, and the painful torment He will inflict upon them.
